sources.entry: LinkedIn Skills by Serge Bulaev - A set of skills for LinkedIn marketing: drafting posts, comments and replies, extracting the hook formula from a viral post, planning a week of content, rewriting a profile, and segmenting the people who engaged. Posts are read through Apify and published through Publora, and every skill shows a draft for approval before anything goes out.

summary.one_liner: A bundle of 12 Claude Code and Codex skills for drafting, auditing, and scheduling LinkedIn posts, comments, and replies, with a draft-for-approval step before anything is published.
summary.what_it_does: Provides 12 skill files that Claude Code, Codex and similar agents load on LinkedIn-related prompts. They draft posts, comments and replies in a set voice, check drafts for AI-style phrasing and algorithm issues, and reverse-engineer hook formulas from viral posts. A Content Planner builds a 7-day plan, and a Profile Optimizer rewrites headline, About, Featured and Experience sections. Engagement Monitor tracks comment threads for author replies and groups likers and commenters by ICP fit. An Interviewer skill builds a Story Bank of the user's experiences that other skills draw on. Optional integrations are Apify for reading posts and engagers, Publora for publishing, and Pixfaro for images; without them, skills fall back to asking the user to paste text or copy drafts.
use_cases: draft a linkedin post in my voice
reply to comments on my linkedin post
plan a week of linkedin content
rewrite my linkedin profile for inbound leads
remove ai-sounding phrasing from a draft
find out who liked or commented on a post
schedule linkedin posts through an API
how_to_run: git clone the repo and open it as the working directory (Claude Code loads skills without plugin install)
notable: Every skill shows a draft and waits for approval before anything is posted
Founder layer with founder-specific angles, extra hook formulas and a founders-edition content plan
Handles LinkedIn's 2-level comment thread flattening when replying
Humanizer sub-tools include an AI-emoji density scorer and a multi-detector spread tester
Works on claude.ai via a connector and with a plain git clone; has a selftest script that reports which integrations are connected
caveats: Auto-posting needs a paid Publora account for anything beyond the free tier (15 posts per month), plus a Publora API key or connector
Reading posts and engagers via Apify uses paid actors (about $1 to $5 per 1,000 results) and needs an Apify token or connector
On claude.ai, skills need a paid Claude plan with code execution enabled
On Windows, a plain clone may load no skills because the .claude/skills mirror uses symlinks; a fix is required
